paragraphs.text: And I, brethren, when I came unto you, came not with excellency of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.
paragraphs.original: Κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἦλθον οὐ καθʼ ὑπεροχὴν λόγου ἢ σοφίας καταγγέλλων ὑμῖν τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kagō elthōn pros hymas, adelphoi, ēlthon ou kathʼ hyperochēn logou ē sophias katangellōn hymin to martyrion tou theou.

paragraphs.text: For I determined not to know anything among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ἔκρινά τι εἰδέναι ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ μὴ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τοῦτον ἐσταυρωμένον·
paragraphs.translit: ou gar ekrina ti eidenai en hymin ei mē Iēsoun Christon kai touton estaurōmenon·

paragraphs.text: And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.
paragraphs.original: κἀγὼ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν φόβῳ καὶ ἐν τρόμῳ πολλῷ ἐγενόμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
paragraphs.translit: kagō en astheneia kai en phobō kai en tromō pollō egenomēn pros hymas,

paragraphs.text: And my speech and my preaching were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ λόγος μου καὶ τὸ κήρυγμά μου οὐκ ἐν πειθοῖ σοφίας ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀποδείξει πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho logos mou kai to kērygma mou ouk en peithoi sophias allʼ en apodeixei pneumatos kai dynameōs,

paragraphs.text: that your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν μὴ ᾖ ἐν σοφίᾳ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλʼ ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hina hē pistis hymōn mē ē en sophia anthrōpōn allʼ en dynamei theou.

paragraphs.text: We speak wisdom, however, among them that are fullgrown: yet a wisdom not of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, who are coming to nought:
paragraphs.original: Σοφίαν δὲ λαλοῦμεν ἐν τοῖς τελείοις, σοφίαν δὲ οὐ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου οὐδὲ τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου τῶν καταργουμένων·
paragraphs.translit: Sophian de laloumen en tois teleiois, sophian de ou tou aiōnos toutou oude tōn archontōn tou aiōnos toutou tōn katargoumenōn·

paragraphs.text: but we speak God`s wisdom in a mystery, [even] the [wisdom] that hath been hidden, which God foreordained before the worlds unto our glory:
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ λαλοῦμεν θεοῦ σοφίαν ἐν μυστηρίῳ, τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην, ἣν προώρισεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων εἰς δόξαν ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: alla laloumen theou sophian en mystēriō, tēn apokekrymmenēn, hēn proōrisen ho theos pro tōn aiōnōn eis doxan hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: which none of the rulers of this world hath known: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory:
paragraphs.original: ἣν οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἔγνωκεν, εἰ γὰρ ἔγνωσαν, οὐκ ἂν τὸν κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν·
paragraphs.translit: hēn oudeis tōn archontōn tou aiōnos toutou egnōken, ei gar egnōsan, ouk an ton kyrion tēs doxēs estaurōsan·

paragraphs.text: but as it is written, Things which eye saw not, and ear heard not, And [which] entered not into the heart of man, Whatsoever things God prepared for them that love him.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἃ ὀφθαλμὸς οὐκ εἶδεν καὶ οὖς οὐκ ἤκουσεν καὶ ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἀνέβη, ὅσα ἡτοίμασεν ὁ θεὸς τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: alla kathōs gegraptai· Ha ophthalmos ouk eiden kai ous ouk ēkousen kai epi kardian anthrōpou ouk anebē, hosa hētoimasen ho theos tois agapōsin auton.

paragraphs.text: But unto us God revealed [them] through the Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.
paragraphs.original: ἡμῖν γὰρ ἀπεκάλυψεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος, τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα πάντα ἐραυνᾷ, καὶ τὰ βάθη τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hēmin gar apekalypsen ho theos dia tou pneumatos, to gar pneuma panta erauna, kai ta bathē tou theou.

paragraphs.text: For who among men knoweth the things of a man, save the spirit of the man, which is in him? even so the things of God none knoweth, save the Spirit of God.
paragraphs.original: τίς γὰρ οἶδεν ἀνθρώπων τὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ; οὕτως καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐδεὶς ἔγνωκεν εἰ μὴ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tis gar oiden anthrōpōn ta tou anthrōpou ei mē to pneuma tou anthrōpou to en autō; houtōs kai ta tou theou oudeis egnōken ei mē to pneuma tou theou.

paragraphs.text: But we received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is from God; that we might know the things that were freely given to us of God.
paragraphs.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐ τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ κόσμου ἐλάβομεν ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα εἰδῶμεν τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ χαρισθέντα ἡμῖν·
paragraphs.translit: hēmeis de ou to pneuma tou kosmou elabomen alla to pneuma to ek tou theou, hina eidōmen ta hypo tou theou charisthenta hēmin·

paragraphs.text: Which things also we speak, not in words which man`s wisdom teacheth, but which the Spirit teacheth; combining spiritual things with spiritual [words].
paragraphs.original: ἃ καὶ λαλοῦμεν οὐκ ἐν διδακτοῖς ἀνθρωπίνης σοφίας λόγοις, ἀλλʼ ἐν διδακτοῖς πνεύματος, πνευματικοῖς πνευματικὰ συγκρίνοντες.
paragraphs.translit: ha kai laloumen ouk en didaktois anthrōpinēs sophias logois, allʼ en didaktois pneumatos, pneumatikois pneumatika synkrinontes.

paragraphs.text: Now the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him; and he cannot know them, because they are spiritually judged.
paragraphs.original: Ψυχικὸς δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ δέχεται τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ, μωρία γὰρ αὐτῷ ἐστίν, καὶ οὐ δύναται γνῶναι, ὅτι πνευματικῶς ἀνακρίνεται·
paragraphs.translit: Psychikos de anthrōpos ou dechetai ta tou pneumatos tou theou, mōria gar autō estin, kai ou dynatai gnōnai, hoti pneumatikōs anakrinetai·

paragraphs.text: But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, and he himself is judged of no man.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ πνευματικὸς ἀνακρίνει τὰ πάντα, αὐτὸς δὲ ὑπʼ οὐδενὸς ἀνακρίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: ho de pneumatikos anakrinei ta panta, autos de hypʼ oudenos anakrinetai.

paragraphs.text: For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he should instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.
paragraphs.original: τίς γὰρ ἔγνω νοῦν κυρίου, ὃς συμβιβάσει αὐτόν; ἡμεῖς δὲ νοῦν Χριστοῦ ἔχομεν.
paragraphs.translit: tis gar egnō noun kyriou, hos symbibasei auton; hēmeis de noun Christou echomen.
